lesson.title: Before this lecture
lesson.lead: Lecture 12's recipe, plus the SVD from Lecture 5 for one board.

items: **Lecture 12, type 1:** centre → S → eigen → unit PCs → scores. Do Practice Paper Q5 first if it is not automatic.
**SVD (Lecture 5):** A = UΣVᵀ, σ² = eigenvalues of AᵀA. Needed only for the SVD board.
λ = 4, 2, 1. Share of the top two? → *Answer:* 6/7 ≈ 85.71%.
Unit PC q₁ = (1, 1)/√2, centred point (2, 0). Its code z? → *Answer:* 2/√2 = √2.
Rebuild from that one code? → *Answer:* √2 · (1, 1)/√2 = (1, 1).

lesson.title: Type 3 · Reduce and reconstruct: the key steps in practice

items: **Mean subtraction** (p. 18): centre each column.
**Standardisation** (p. 19): divide each column by its standard deviation σ_d, when columns are in different units (see the slide example in Lecture 12: x₂ swamps x₁).
**Eigendecomposition** (p. 21): S, its eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors; sort by λ.
**Projection** (p. 22–23): a new point x* is standardised with the **training** μ and σ, then z* = Bᵀx*, x̃* = BBᵀx*.

groups.label: Code and rebuild
groups.note: B = [b₁ … b_M]: the M top eigenvectors as columns. BᵀB = I, but BBᵀ ≠ I (it is the projector).

groups.label: How much is kept
groups.note: Choose the smallest M that reaches the target (90%, 95%).

groups.label: How much is lost
lines: ‖x − x̃‖² = sum of its squared scores on the dropped PCs

groups.label: Components are uncorrelated
groups.note: Off-diagonal 0: the new features carry no repeated information.

blocks.label: Where marks are lost
blocks.text: Keeping PCs in the order they appear in S instead of by λ · standardising a test point with its own statistics · forgetting to add μ back · expecting BBᵀ = I.

items: **Read:** `Lecture_13.pdf` p. 17–25; Companion §10–§11.
**Do:** P42, Companion Q3, Companion Q6.

lesson.title: Type 4 · Wide data: when D ≫ N
lesson.lead: `Lecture_13.pdf` p. 14–16 and Companion §9. Asked in 2022 makeup Q3(2).

blocks.text: **The problem:** S is D × D. With 12,000 features that is a 1 GB matrix and about D³ work, for only a few dozen points. **The trick:** the small N × N matrix has the same non-zero eigenvalues.

groups.label: Points as columns (slides)
groups.note: Find cₘ from the small matrix, then bₘ = Xcₘ/‖Xcₘ‖.

groups.label: Points as rows (P43, Companion)
groups.note: Same idea, X transposed. Check the shapes: the small matrix is always N × N.

items: At most N − 1 eigenvalues are non-zero (centring removes one degree of freedom).
Always **normalise** Xc (or Xᵀu).
To turn an eigenvalue of XXᵀ (without 1/N) into a variance, divide by N.
**Read:** `Lecture_13.pdf` p. 14–16; Companion §9.
**Do:** P43, then 2022 makeup Q3(2).

lesson.title: Type 5 · The SVD route and low-rank approximation

groups.label: Eigenvalues from singular values
groups.note: Slides store points as columns: the PCs are the columns of **U**. With points as rows (Companion Q7) they are the columns of **V**. Pick the factor whose vectors have D entries.

groups.label: Best rank-M approximation (Eckart–Young)
lines: U_M Σ_M V_Mᵀ   (keep the M largest σ)

blocks.text: **Why software uses the SVD:** forming XᵀX squares the numbers and loses precision; the SVD of X gives the same PCs without it.

items: **Read:** `Lecture_13.pdf` p. 5–9.

lesson.title: Type 6 · Practical aspects and reasoning questions
lesson.lead: `Lecture_13.pdf` p. 10–13 and Companion §13. Short "justify" questions in the older papers.

head: Question
One-line answer
Asked in
rows: Why not solve det(S − λI) = 0 for big S?
No formula for polynomial roots of degree ≥ 5 (Abel–Ruffini, p. 11): software iterates.
Power iteration xₖ₊₁ = Sxₖ/‖Sxₖ‖ converges to the top eigenvector (p. 13).
Data rotated and shifted (y = Qx + μ)?
PCs become Qbⱼ, same λ, same shares; μ has no effect.
PCs change: RS is not orthogonal, so Rbᵢ are not the new PCs.
Can PC1 always separate two classes?
No: PCA ignores labels (thin gap along the small direction).
Arbitrary: v and −v are both unit eigenvectors; scores flip sign.
Standardise first, or the large-unit feature becomes PC1.

items: **Read:** `Lecture_13.pdf` p. 10–13; Companion §13.
**Do:** previous batch Q5, then skim the three older reasoning questions.

worked.title: Reduce · Sourabh P42: keeping two of three components

problem.text: Centred 3-feature data have covariance S = [[3, 1, 0], [1, 3, 0], [0, 0, 1]]. A centred point is x = (2, 0, 1). (a) Eigenvalues and unit eigenvectors of S. (b) Fraction of total variance kept by the top two PCs. (c) The 2-D code z and the reconstruction x̃. (d) The reconstruction error ‖x − x̃‖ and the average squared error over the data. (Saurabh sir's `MFML_ZC416_Solved_Practice_Set.pdf`)

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Codes z = Bᵀx, rebuilds x̃ = Bz, and "average error = sum of the dropped eigenvalues".

steps.label: Plan of attack
steps.text: S is block-diagonal: do the 2 × 2 block and the lone 1 separately. Sort by λ. Code, rebuild, subtract.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: Saurabh sir's symbols: qᵢ = unit eigenvectors, Q_k = [q₁ … q_k], z = code, x̃ = reconstruction.

steps.label: STEP 5 · (d) Error
steps.text:
x − x̃ = (0, 0, 1) ⇒ ‖x − x̃‖ = **1**
Average squared error over the data = dropped eigenvalue λ₃ = **1**

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Keeping the PCs in the order they appear in S instead of by eigenvalue.
• Forgetting to multiply back by Q_k for the reconstruction.

worked.priorityWhy: The one Saurabh sir problem for codes and reconstruction

worked.title: Reduce · Companion Q3: projecting a new observation (5 marks)

problem.text: Training means μ = (4, 10), standard deviations σ = (2, 5). On standardised data the kept component is α₁ = (3/5, 4/5) and the dropped one α₂ = (−4/5, 3/5). New point x* = (6, 20). (a) Standardise x*, saying which μ, σ you use. [1M] (b) Score z* = α₁ᵀx* and reconstruction x̃* = α₁α₁ᵀx* (standardised scale). [2M] (c) Squared reconstruction error; check it equals the squared score on α₂. [2M] (Companion §15, Question 3)

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: The slides' last two steps (`Lecture_13.pdf` p. 22–23): standardise with the **training** statistics, then project.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: Companion symbols: α₁, α₂ = unit PCs, z* = score, x̃* = reconstruction.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) Standardise  [1M]
steps.text:
Use the training μ and σ (a single new point has no mean of its own):
x*(std) = ((6 − 4)/2, (20 − 10)/5) = **(1, 2)**

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Standardising the new point with its own values or with test statistics.
• Forgetting that x̃* is on the standardised scale (undo with σ and μ only if asked).

worked.priorityWhy: The one problem for a new point (slides p. 22–23)

worked.title: Reduce · Companion Q6: how many components, and why they are uncorrelated (5 marks)

problem.text: Σ has eigenvalues 4.5, 2.1, 0.9, 0.4, 0.1. (a) Total variance and tr Σ. [1M] (b) Share of the first two PCs; the fewest PCs for at least 90%. [2M] (c) With W = all five unit eigenvectors and Z = XW, show Cov(Z) is diagonal; what are its entries? [2M] (Companion §15, Question 6)

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Eigenvalues as a variance budget; choosing M; decorrelation.

steps.label: STEP 3 · (c) Cov(Z)
steps.text:
Cov(Z) = (1/N)(XW)ᵀ(XW) = WᵀΣW
ΣW = WΛ and WᵀW = I ⇒ Cov(Z) = WᵀWΛ = **Λ = diag(4.5, 2.1, 0.9, 0.4, 0.1)**
Off-diagonal zeros ⇒ the components are **uncorrelated**; each variance is its λ.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: 8.0; 82.5%, M = 3; Cov(Z) = diag(λ): uncorrelated components.

worked.priorityWhy: The one problem for choosing M and % variance

worked.title: Reduce · Companion Q4: three variables, reading the structure first (6 marks)

problem.text: Σ = [[4, 2, 0], [2, 4, 0], [0, 0, 3]]. (a) Without the full cubic, find all eigenvalues; check with tr and det. [2M] (b) The three unit eigenvectors; check they are orthogonal. [2M] (c) Y₁ and Var(Y₁); keeping Y₁ and Y₂, which variable is rebuilt exactly and what is lost? [2M] (Companion §15, Question 4)

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Using zeros in Σ: a variable uncorrelated with the rest gives its own eigenvalue.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) Eigenvalues
steps.text:
X₃ is uncorrelated with X₁, X₂ ⇒ λ = 3 directly.
Block [[4, 2], [2, 4]]: λ = 4 ± 2 = 6, 2
Sorted **6, 3, 2**; 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 = tr ✓; 6·3·2 = 36 = 3·(16 − 4) = det ✓

steps.label: STEP 3 · (c)
steps.text:
Y₁ = (X₁ + X₂)/√2, Var = 6
Keep α₁, α₂: x̃ = ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (x₁ + x₂)/2, x₃) ⇒ x₃ rebuilt exactly; x₁, x₂ replaced by their average.
Lost: (X₁ − X₂)/√2 with variance (4 + 4 − 2·2)/2 = 2 = λ₃ ✓

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: λ = 6, 3, 2; α₁ = (1, 1, 0)/√2, α₂ = (0, 0, 1), α₃ = (1, −1, 0)/√2; the difference X₁ − X₂ is lost (variance 2).

worked.answer: λ = 6, 3, 2; the lost part is (X₁ − X₂)/√2 with variance 2.
worked.priorityWhy: Extra practice of a type a must-do problem already covers

worked.title: Wide data · Sourabh P43: PCA through the N × N Gram matrix

problem.text: Three centred observations in ℝ⁴ are the rows of X = [[1, 1, 0, 2], [1, −1, 2, 0], [−2, 0, −2, −2]]. Avoid the 4 × 4 covariance. (a) Check the data are centred; K = XXᵀ. (b) Verify (1, 1, −2), (1, −1, 0), (1, 1, 1) are eigenvectors of K; eigenvalues? (c) First principal direction u₁ = Xᵀv₁/‖Xᵀv₁‖. (d) Variance along u₁ (S = (1/N)XᵀX) and the rank of S. (Saurabh sir's `MFML_ZC416_Solved_Practice_Set.pdf`)

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: XXᵀ and XᵀX share their non-zero eigenvalues (`Lecture_13.pdf` p. 14–16).

steps.label: Plan of attack
steps.text: Build the small K → test the given vectors → Xᵀv → normalise → divide λ by N.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: Saurabh sir stores points as **rows** here, so K = XXᵀ is N × N (3 × 3) and S = (1/N)XᵀX is D × D (4 × 4).

steps.label: STEP 4 · (d)
steps.text:
Variance along u₁ = λ/N = 18/3 = **6**
S has non-zero eigenvalues 18/3 = 6 and 6/3 = 2 ⇒ **rank 2**

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text:
• Using Xᵀv without normalising.
• Forgetting to divide by N to turn an eigenvalue of K into a variance.

worked.priorityWhy: The one Saurabh sir problem for wide data

worked.title: Wide data · Companion Q5: 12,000 genes, 40 samples (6 marks)

problem.text: D = 12,000 genes, N = 40 samples; centred X is 40 × 12,000 (rows = samples), Σ = (1/N)XᵀX. (a) Size and memory of Σ (8-byte doubles); why not eigendecompose it directly? [2M] (b) Show that if Σw = λw then u = Xw satisfies Ku = λu with K = (1/N)XXᵀ; size of K? [2M] (c) Recover w from u; the largest possible number of non-zero eigenvalues of Σ? [2M] (Companion §15, Question 5)

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: The size argument and the two-line proof of the trick.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a)
steps.text: Σ is 12,000 × 12,000 = 1.44 × 10⁸ entries × 8 bytes ≈ **1.15 GB**; eigendecomposition costs about D³ ≈ 1.7 × 10¹² operations.

steps.label: STEP 2 · (b)
steps.text: (1/N)XᵀXw = λw ⇒ multiply by X: (1/N)XXᵀ(Xw) = λ(Xw) ⇒ **Ku = λu**, K is **40 × 40**, same λ.

steps.label: STEP 3 · (c)
steps.text:
Multiply Ku = λu by Xᵀ: Σ(Xᵀu) = λ(Xᵀu) ⇒ **w = Xᵀu/‖Xᵀu‖**
rank ≤ N − 1 = **39** (centring removes one degree of freedom) ⇒ at most 39 non-zero eigenvalues.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: 1.15 GB; Ku = λu with K 40 × 40; w = Xᵀu/‖Xᵀu‖; at most 39 non-zero λ.

worked.answer: K = (1/N)XXᵀ is 40 × 40 with the same λ; w = Xᵀu/‖Xᵀu‖; ≤ 39 non-zero.
worked.priorityWhy: Extra practice of a type a must-do problem already covers

worked.title: Wide data · 2022 makeup Q3(2): eig() only works below 32 rows (3 marks)

problem.text: x₁, …, x₂₀ ∈ ℝ¹⁰²⁴ and S = Σxᵢxᵢᵀ (1024 × 1024). A function eig() only handles symmetric matrices with fewer than 32 rows. (a) How do you get the eigenvalues of S? [1.5M] (b) The eigenvectors? [1.5M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: The same trick with points as columns.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: Here X = [x₁ … x₂₀] has the points as **columns** (1024 × 20), so S = XXᵀ and the small matrix is XᵀX (20 × 20).

steps.label: STEP 1 · Use the small matrix  [0.5M]
steps.text: XᵀX is 20 × 20 < 32 rows ⇒ eig() can handle it.

steps.label: STEP 2 · (a) Eigenvalues  [1M]
steps.text: XᵀXc = λc ⇒ multiply by X: XXᵀ(Xc) = λ(Xc). So the eigenvalues of XᵀX are the non-zero eigenvalues of S; the other 1004 are 0.

steps.label: STEP 3 · (b) Eigenvectors  [1.5M]
steps.text: [P, D] = eig(XᵀX); for each column c of P, **d = Xc** (normalised d/‖d‖) is an eigenvector of S with the same λ.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: eig(XᵀX): same non-zero eigenvalues; eigenvectors Xc/‖Xc‖.

steps.label: More
steps.text: Whole paper: [Exam hall · 2022 makeup Q3](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/p-es-mkp-2022/worked/3).

worked.answer: Use eig(XᵀX): same λ, eigenvectors Xc/‖Xc‖.
worked.priorityWhy: Older paper: the same recipe as the must-do problems

worked.title: SVD · Companion Q7: from singular values to components (6 marks)

problem.text: Centred X has N = 100 rows, D = 4 columns, singular values 20, 10, 5, 1. (a) Eigenvalues of Σ = (1/N)XᵀX; where are the principal directions in X = UΣₛVᵀ? [2M] (b) Share of the first two PCs; the fewest PCs for at least 95%. [2M] (c) Best rank-2 approximation; its error in the spectral and Frobenius norms. [2M] (Companion §15, Question 7)

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: λ = σ²/N (`Lecture_13.pdf` p. 6–7) and Eckart–Young (p. 8–9).

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: Σₛ = the diagonal matrix of singular values (to keep it apart from the covariance Σ). Points are rows here, so the directions are the columns of **V**. (The slides store points as columns and find them in U.)

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) λ = σ²/N
steps.text:
λ = 400/100, 100/100, 25/100, 1/100 = **4, 1, 0.25, 0.01**
Principal directions = columns of V (they live in feature space, D = 4 entries).

steps.label: STEP 3 · (c) Eckart–Young
steps.text:
X̃₂ = σ₁u₁v₁ᵀ + σ₂u₂v₂ᵀ (truncate the SVD)
Spectral error = σ₃ = **5**; Frobenius error = √(σ₃² + σ₄²) = √26 ≈ **5.10**

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: λ = 4, 1, 0.25, 0.01 (columns of V); 95.06%, M = 2; X̃₂ = U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ, errors 5 and √26.

worked.priorityWhy: The one problem for the SVD route

worked.title: Reasoning · Previous batch Q5: PCA after a rotation and a shift

problem.text: PCA on x₁, …, x_N gives directions b₁, …, b_D. The data become yᵢ = Qxᵢ + μ with QᵀQ = I and μ constant. Find the new principal components in terms of the old ones. How much variance does the first PC capture compared with before?

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: How the covariance and its eigenvectors change under y = Qx + μ. The same idea answers 2023 Q4(D) (rotating the points).

steps.label: STEP 1 · The shift disappears
steps.text: ȳ = Qx̄ + μ ⇒ yᵢ − ȳ = Q(xᵢ − x̄): μ has no effect.

steps.label: STEP 2 · New covariance
steps.text: S_y = (1/N)Σ Q(xᵢ − x̄)(xᵢ − x̄)ᵀQᵀ = **QS_xQᵀ**

steps.label: STEP 3 · New eigenvectors
steps.text: S_y(Qbⱼ) = QS_xQᵀQbⱼ = QS_xbⱼ = λⱼ(Qbⱼ) ⇒ new PCs are **Qbⱼ**, same eigenvalues.

steps.label: STEP 4 · Variance
steps.text: λ₁ unchanged and tr S_y = tr S_x ⇒ PC1 captures **the same amount and the same share**.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: PCs Qbⱼ, eigenvalues unchanged, μ irrelevant, same variance for PC1.

steps.label: More
steps.text: Whole paper: [Exam hall · previous batch](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/p-es-prev-2023/worked/4).

worked.answer: New PCs Qbⱼ; same eigenvalues; same share.
worked.priorityWhy: The one problem for how a change of the data moves the PCs

worked.title: Reasoning · 2022 regular Q1(a–b): what scaling the features does (8 marks)

problem.text: (a) Every point (x₁, …, x_D) becomes (α₁x₁, …, α_Dx_D). Is it enough to scale each old eigenvector the same way? [5M] (b) Given the old covariance, can the new one be computed in O(D²)? [3M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Scaling is **not** a rotation: the PCs really change.

steps.label: Notation
steps.text: R = diag(α₁, …, α_D); points as columns of X; SΛSᵀ = old covariance's eigendecomposition. Here αᵢ are scaling constants.

steps.label: STEP 1 · (a) New covariance  [3M]
steps.text: X ↦ RX ⇒ new covariance R XXᵀ R = RSΛSᵀR

steps.label: STEP 2 · (a) Why it fails  [2M]
steps.text:
(RS)(RS)ᵀ = R² ≠ I (unless every αᵢ = ±1) ⇒ RS is not orthogonal, so Rbᵢ are not the new PCs.
Check: PCs (1, 1), (1, −1) of [[2, 1], [1, 2]] scaled by diag(1, 2) give (1, 2) and (1, −2), whose dot product is −3 ≠ 0: they are not even perpendicular. **He is wrong.**

steps.label: STEP 3 · (b) O(D²)  [3M]
steps.text: (RSR)ᵢⱼ = αᵢSᵢⱼαⱼ: D² entries, 2 multiplications each ⇒ **O(D²), yes**.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: (a) No: RS is not orthogonal. (b) Yes: αᵢSᵢⱼαⱼ in O(D²).

steps.label: More
steps.text: Whole paper: [Exam hall · 2022 regular Q1](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/p-es-reg-2022/worked/1).

worked.title: Reasoning · Sep 2024 makeup Q3(B): can PC1 always separate two classes? (2 marks)

problem.text: Data points belong to two classes. Is it always true that, after projecting onto PC1, the classes can be separated by a threshold? [2M]

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: PCA never looks at the labels.

steps.label: STEP 1 · Answer
steps.text: **No.** PC1 follows the largest variance, not the class split.

steps.label: STEP 2 · Counter-example
steps.text: Class A at (x, +0.1), class B at (x, −0.1) for x from −10 to 10. PC1 is the x-axis; both classes project onto the same range −10 … 10, so no threshold separates them, though the line y = 0 does.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: No; a wide cloud split by a thin gap along the small-variance direction.

steps.label: More
steps.text: Whole question: [Exam hall · Sep 2024 makeup Q3](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/p-es-mkp-2024/worked/3).

worked.title: Reasoning · Sep 2024 regular Q3(B): the power method (2 marks)

problem.text: A = diag(2, 4, 4); power method from x = (0, 0.5, 1). Which eigenvalue and eigenvector does it converge to? [2M] (`Lecture_13.pdf` p. 13: xₖ₊₁ = Sxₖ/‖Sxₖ‖)

steps.label: What is tested
steps.text: Power iteration finds the eigenvector of the largest eigenvalue.

steps.label: STEP 1 · One step
steps.text: Ax = (0, 2, 4) = 4(0, 0.5, 1): the start is already an eigenvector.

steps.label: STEP 2 · Answer
steps.text: Converges at once to **λ = 4** with eigenvector (0, 0.5, 1) (normalised (0, 1, 2)/√5). λ = 4 is repeated, so any vector of span{(0, 1, 0), (0, 0, 1)} is an eigenvector too.

steps.label: Answers at a glance
steps.text: λ = 4, eigenvector (0, 0.5, 1).

steps.label: More
steps.text: Whole question: [Exam hall · Sep 2024 regular Q3](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/p-es-reg-2024/worked/3).
